Within a label, coverage at a fixed threshold depends only on how that label's tracings score, so sinus rhythm in the old, and right bundle-branch block in the young, score further from their thresholds than at the source; this study does not measure why. Between the sexes the median gap {{rot.uncertainty.sex_median}} and the {{rot.uncertainty.sex_widest}}. At Columbia, the coverage of the ill outpatients is {{women}} for women and {{men}} for men.

## Appendix H. How the cut-offs are computed, the reweighted option and the intervals

Both conformal schemes score a case by one minus the probability the model gives its label, the least-ambiguous-set score, and admit a label when that score falls at or below the ⌈(n+1)(1−α)⌉/n empirical quantile of the calibration scores, with α = 0.10 for the 90% target; the (n+1) is what makes the guarantee hold in finite samples rather than asymptotically. The single threshold and per-label calibration meet at the same miss rate on the ill by construction and not by measurement: the per-label threshold of the ill admits the disease above the point below which 10% of the ill calibration cases' scores fall, which is the single threshold's 90%-sensitivity point, the two taking the same finite-sample rank of the same scores.

Since two label probabilities sum to one, a set comes back empty only when the two thresholds admitting each label sum to less than one. At α = 0.10 on the infarction model they do not: the pooled scheme puts a single threshold at {{thr.pooled_upper}}, and the per-label pair sits at {{thr.q0}} and {{thr.q1}}, summing to {{d.thr_sum}}. Every referral in the pooled and per-label schemes is therefore a both-label set; the weighted scheme is the exception. At an 80% target the two thresholds sum to less than one, so every deferral is an empty set rather than a both-label set, {{ab.empty_80}} of tracings at the source. Under the adaptive-prediction-sets score, also in the results files, the source-site infarction coverage reads {{ab.aps_mi}} against {{ab.lac_mi}}, bought with a much larger deferral rate.

The fourth scheme, label-shift weighting, reweights the calibration cases toward the target's class mix estimated by black-box shift estimation [26], with an asymptotic guarantee that depends on that estimate [3,4]; it was run on infarction and on the rotation. Its estimate was poor: {{wt.acs.estimate}} infarction at Chongqing against {{inf.acs_prevalence}} observed, and {{wt.sph.estimate}} at Shandong against {{inf.sph_prevalence}}. Reweighting also spends calibration data, the effective sample size falling from {{wt.calibration_n}} to {{wt.acs.ess}} at Chongqing and {{wt.sph.ess}} at Shandong. Paired on the same draws it gained {{wt.ptbxl.gain}} points of infarction coverage at the source where per-label calibration gained {{wt.ptbxl.mondrian_gain}}, and at Shandong it lost {{wt.sph.loss}} points and produced empty sets on {{s.weighted.sph.empty}} of tracings. An asymptotic guarantee resting on an estimated prior bought nothing here that an exact construction resting on none did not buy more cheaply.

For infarction, the spread across the 200 draws describes the calibration draw, not the sampling error of the cohorts, which is the larger quantity at the target sites. Where a claim rests on a difference, the interval comes from 2,000 replicates that resample the source patients before halving them and resample each target cohort as well, by record, since the score files carry no patient identifier; the scored cohorts are {{inf.sph_n}} tracings from {{s.sph_patients}} patients at Shandong and {{inf.acs_n}} from {{s.acs_patients}} at Chongqing. Named tests fail if a record-level split replaces the patient-level one, if any target label reaches a threshold, or if a published figure differs from its recomputation by an implementation that does not import the one under test. The quantities the discussion argues from (the plain reject rule, the finite-sample correction, the cases a site needs to measure its own coverage, the predictive value and AUROC at each site) are computed by `scripts/auxiliary.py` into `results/auxiliary.json`.

On EchoNext, intervals on a share are 95% Wilson intervals, and on an AUROC 95% bootstrap intervals over 500 draws; the severity reweighting's intervals come from {{sev.draws}} bootstrap draws. The coverage of the ill outpatients is {{women}} ({{women_ci}}) for women and {{men}} ({{men_ci}}) for men.

A bootstrap that resamples the infarction cohorts leaves the differences this study rests on intact, the per-label gain over pooled calibration in infarction coverage at +{{diff.ptbxl}} points at the source, 95% interval {{diff.ptbxl_ci}}, and +{{diff.acs}} at Chongqing, {{diff.acs_ci}}, while widening the intervals on the individual levels at the source to {{diff.ptbxl_pooled_ci}} for pooled calibration and {{diff.ptbxl_perlabel_ci}} for per-label; those two remain separated. At Shandong the 95% Wilson interval on pooled infarction coverage sits {{w.sph_wilson_below}} points below the estimate and {{w.sph_wilson_above}} above.

## Appendix I. The recording faults

`scripts/perturbations.py` writes `results/perturbations.json`; its unperturbed condition is scored through the same path and agrees with `results/baseline/scores.npz` to {{p.clean_agreement}} × 10⁻⁷, so the differences are the fault's and not the pipeline's.

Scaling every lead by 0.8 left the AUROC unchanged to four decimals while {{p.gain.moved}} of the {{inf.fold10}} records changed rank, Kendall's tau between the two score vectors being {{p.gain.tau}}. The reordering is local and cancels over pairs: {{p.gain.pairs_flipped}} of infarction and non-infarction pairs flip, in both directions, and the AUROC moves by {{p.gain.auroc_fifth}} in the fifth decimal. The whole distribution moved, the median score rising from {{p.gain.median_clean}} to {{p.gain.median}}, so the threshold left where it was cut it somewhere else.

Baseline wander is the one fault the deferral rate shows, because it moves the bulk of the distribution onto the deferral band rather than past it: it compresses the scores, the standard deviation falling from {{p.wander.sd_clean}} to {{p.wander.sd}}, and shifts them, the median rising from {{p.wander.median_clean}} to {{p.wander.median}}, so that {{p.wander.between}} of tracings land between the two per-label boundaries against {{p.wander.between_clean}} as recorded.

## Appendix J. Earlier work, with its figures

On a skin-lesion classifier, marginal coverage was met while the melanoma class was under-covered and the nevus class over-covered [12]; two 2026 preprints report the same pattern, and its class-conditional repair, in virtual drug screening and across fifteen imbalanced tabular datasets [5,6]. A 2026 study of intensive-care arrhythmia classification from the photoplethysmogram found marginal coverage at 90.0% with critical-rhythm coverage at 7.5%, raised to 82.5% by class-conditional calibration, and concluded that such systems should be evaluated by per-class and per-patient coverage [14]. On the ECG, a conference abstract by Dzikowicz and colleagues applies split, class-conditional and learn-then-test conformal prediction to acute infarction on PTB-XL, reporting an AUROC of 0.923 without it against 0.932 for split and 0.943 for class-conditional, with overall coverage falling to 84.8% and 86.7%; it uses no other dataset, reports coverage over all cases rather than within each label, and sets no tuned single threshold beside the conformal ones [7]. El Allam and Hamlich, calibrating a quantised classifier for a microcontroller, compared pooled against class-conditional calibration on PTB-XL over ten patient-wise rotations of Normal against infarction at 36.4% infarction: "pooled calibration achieved 91.64% Normal coverage and 88.59% MI coverage; Mondrian calibration achieved 90.65% and 90.53%, reducing the class-coverage gap from 3.06 to 0.12 percentage points" [15]. The minority-label gap at the calibration site, and its repair, are therefore theirs first on this modality. Their second dataset does not reach the question of transfer, and they say so: Chapman-Shaoxing "was evaluated in a separate in-distribution experiment" and "should not be interpreted as evidence of cross-database transfer".

For structural heart disease, the full EchoNext model reaches an AUROC of 84.3% among outpatients and 84.1% among inpatients and in the emergency department [17], and the public mini-model shows no care setting whose AUROC differs significantly from the whole test set [18]. Carried to MIMIC-IV, the mini-model's AUROC for the composite was 0.790 against 0.820 on its own test split, and its probabilities overestimated risk [21]. A per-class threshold need not hold when more than prevalence changes: in magnetic resonance imaging of multiple sclerosis, one calibrated on 3 T scans covered 85.8% of patients at 3 T and 77.5% at 1.5 T for a target of 90% [23].
